events.title: Liberation of Auschwitz
events.description: Soviet Red Army troops of the 60th Army entered the Auschwitz-Birkenau concentration and extermination camp complex in occupied Poland, finding roughly 7,000 emaciated survivors left behind after the Nazis forced tens of thousands of prisoners on death marches.
events.significance: Auschwitz became the symbol of the Holocaust, where over one million people, mostly Jews, were murdered. The date is now observed as International Holocaust Remembrance Day.

events.title: Birth of Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart
events.description: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart was born in Salzburg, in the Archbishopric of Salzburg. A child prodigy, he composed prolifically from the age of five and went on to write over 600 works, including operas, symphonies, concertos and chamber music.
events.significance: Mozart is regarded as one of the greatest composers in Western music history, and his works helped define the Classical style and influenced generations of composers.

events.title: Apollo 1 Fire
events.description: During a launch rehearsal test at Cape Kennedy, a fire broke out in the command module of Apollo 1, killing astronauts Virgil 'Gus' Grissom, Edward White and Roger Chaffee. The cabin's pure oxygen atmosphere and flammable materials contributed to the rapid spread of the fire.
events.significance: The tragedy led to a major redesign of the Apollo spacecraft and stricter safety standards, paving the way for the later success of the Apollo program and the 1969 Moon landing.

events.title: Outer Space Treaty Signed
events.description: The Treaty on Principles Governing the Activities of States in the Exploration and Use of Outer Space, including the Moon and Other Celestial Bodies, was opened for signature in Washington, London and Moscow by the United States, the United Kingdom and the Soviet Union, among others.
events.significance: It established the foundation of international space law, banning nuclear weapons in orbit and declaring that celestial bodies cannot be claimed by any nation.

events.title: Paris Peace Accords Signed
events.description: The United States, North Vietnam, South Vietnam and the Provisional Revolutionary Government signed the Paris Peace Accords, formally ending direct U.S. military involvement in the Vietnam War and providing for a ceasefire and the withdrawal of American troops.
events.significance: The agreement ended U.S. combat involvement in Vietnam after more than a decade, although fighting between North and South continued until the fall of Saigon in 1975.
